Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-5ig0pv_r/call-0702c2210b844cb7b840c06508e19a1b/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3; ls /fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/runtime/pdf'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else 'unavailable')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(p.pages))
print('Metadata:',p.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(p.pages,1):
    s=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(s)
    parts.append(f'\\n--- PAGE {i} ---\\n'+s)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(parts))
print('\\n'.join(parts[:2]))
PY"

strengths: MaskSub provides a simple, technically coherent way to train with strong masking: a masked pass learns from detached predictions of an unmasked pass through the same network. It requires no change to the deployed architecture, making the contribution practically useful.

The main empirical evidence is substantial. Table 1 reports ImageNet improvements of 0.6–0.7 percentage points across ViT sizes at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs. Tables 3 and 5 extend the results to several pretrained models, ResNets, and Swin Transformers using established training recipes.

Compute-matched comparisons support the practical benefit beyond simply spending more computation. In Table 7, ViT-B with MaskSub reaches 84.1% using 25 GPU-days, versus 83.7% using 26 GPU-days for longer baseline training. Table 8 also shows a favorable accuracy–cost comparison with CoSub.

The appendix establishes relevance beyond ImageNet classification. ADE20K segmentation improves by 0.4–0.6 mIoU, and robustness gains occur across multiple benchmarks and model sizes; for example, ViT-B ImageNet-A accuracy increases from 36.8% to 41.9%.

Ablations examine masking ratios, loss weights, distillation, and alternative drop regularizations. Three-run statistics support key ViT-S/B results, while the pseudocode, detailed recipe tables, and supplied code link help reproducibility. Taken together, the supported empirical contribution favors acceptance.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is moderate: detached-target consistency, self-distillation, and MAE-style token removal are established components. The contribution is chiefly their effective integration into supervised training. Furthermore, Table 6 compares methods using different training recipes, so it cannot establish that competing self-distillation approaches are incompatible with strong recipes or isolate MaskSub's superiority over them.

The explanation of 'automatic difficulty control' exceeds the evidence. Equation 3 contains no correctness-based gate, so confidently incorrect unmasked predictions can also provide strong targets. Figure 3's aggregate gradient norms support an optimization pattern, but do not establish the claim that masking is effectively restricted to successfully learned images. This limits the mechanistic interpretation rather than invalidating the objective.

Benefits are not universal. Applying MaskSub during transfer fine-tuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.7% to 89.6% in Table 10. Section 4.2 also states that peak CLIP fine-tuning accuracy matches the baseline, despite improved final-epoch accuracy. These results qualify the broad claims of consistent improvement, particularly given the approximately doubled training cost for hierarchical architectures.

Some supporting evidence remains less conclusive than the main ViT results. The 0.1-point BEiTv2 gains and small detection improvements lack uncertainty estimates. Table A.6 also does not clearly specify whether 'without KD loss' replaces distillation with ground-truth supervision or removes the masked branch's learning signal, limiting interpretation of that control.

There are correctable reporting errors: Section 4.4 claims one-sixth of GradAug's fine-tuning cost, whereas Table 9 gives 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU-days, approximately 37%. Table 10's ViT-S Cars result of 92.2% versus 80.9% implies +11.3 points, not +1.3. These affect reporting precision without overturning the central findings.
